The page image is extremely faint pencil, and almost nothing can be read with confidence. The machine transcription is essentially empty: it gives only fragments and '[?]' markers. A step-by-step reconstruction is therefore impossible, and what follows is a description of what is visible plus a context-based guess, clearly marked as such.

(a) Layout. The upper third holds a block of about four long equations. Their right-hand sides contain a factor written as a bracket, roughly (A/(x..) - (B Delta/x..)*x), multiplied by a parenthesized linear combination of elastic constants. A symbol X is defined at the right end of line 4: 'X = ...'. Below that, on the right, a column of about three equations is each of the form (two fractions) * (constant combination) = (difference of two fractions). The middle of the page has two long equations starting at the left margin, of the form '... = X(...) + (...)(...) + ...'. The lower half holds a sequence of equations involving terms written like 'Pi_xx' or 'pi_{xx}' (possibly a stress-component notation), a 'mu Delta' term on the right, and the symbol phi. The last line reads approximately: (A/x.. - B/x.. * x)(const) + (C/x.. - D/x.. * x)(const)*zeta - ... = X(const).

(b) Context (my inference, not read from this page). The previous page, 79r, is a computation in linear isotropic elasticity. It uses the Lame constants lambda and mu, the Laplacian Delta^2, rho = distance (the transcriber's '1/varrho' is 1/r), and the depth coordinate zeta. Coefficients 4(lambda+mu)zeta, 4(lambda+2mu) and 4(lambda+3mu) multiply derivatives of 1/r. That is the structure of Kelvin's point-force solution and of the Boussinesq/Cerruti-type half-space solutions built from it. On 79r Riemann integrates Delta^2 r = 2/r to get (lambda+mu) rho = -4(lambda+mu) zeta d^2 rho/dx^2 + 2(lambda+3mu) d rho/dx, and he introduces chi = x Delta^2 rho - 2 d rho/dx.

(c) Reading this page in that light (inference). The recurring factor that the machine transcription reads as '(lambda+lambda')' is almost certainly one of the combinations (lambda+mu), (lambda+2mu) or (lambda+3mu). The glyph read as '8' after the bracket on the last lines is very probably zeta, matching '(lambda+mu)zeta' on 79r. The page thus most likely continues the same calculation: it determines the component functions (X, phi, and possibly stresses Pi_xx) of a displacement or stress field due to a concentrated force. The likely method is to collect terms in (lambda+mu), (lambda+2mu) and zeta and match them against the boundary condition at the surface.
